name: TX-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Joaquin Castro, a well-known Democratic figure, runs in a D+16 San Antonio district
Challenger Edgardo Baez is badly outspent, with about $6,000 on hand versus Castro's $145,000
No public polls or expert ratings list the race; Polymarket prices Castro near 96% to win
No outside spending on either side and no competitive primary signals
model.rationale: This race rests on fundamentals: a D+16 district, a veteran incumbent with a commanding money advantage, and a first-time challenger with minimal resources. Markets price Castro near-certain, and nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive general election.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Castro or a major candidate-specific surprise would be the main threat, though neither appears likely to put the seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-20 centers on San Antonio and has voted Democratic by wide margins in recent cycles. Joaquin Castro, a longtime incumbent and a prominent national Democratic figure, is seeking another term. Edgardo Rafael Baez, the Republican nominee, is a first-time candidate with little financial backing. No public polling of the general election is available, and expert rating outlets have not listed the race as competitive.

The financial gap is stark. Castro has raised about $586,000 and holds roughly $145,000, while Baez has raised about $67,000 with only $6,000 remaining. No outside groups have advertised on either side, and there are no signs of a contested Democratic primary. Prediction markets give Castro roughly a 96% chance of winning. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with Castro expected to carry the district by a margin in the low-to-mid twenties.
